(a) In General.—Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and every 90 days thereafter until January 1, 2020, the Secretary of the Navy shall provide to the congressional defense committees information on efforts by the Navy’s Physiological Episode Team to combat the prevalence of 
physiological episodes in F/A–18 Hornet and Super Hornet, EA–18G Growler, and T–45 Goshawk aircraft. 
    (b) Elements.—The information required under subsection (a) shall include the following elements:
        (1) A description of Naval Aviation Enterprise activities addressing physiological episodes during the reporting period. 
        (2) An estimate of funding expended in support of the activities described under paragraph (1). 
        (3) A description of any planned or executed changes to Physiological Episode Team structure or processes. 
        (4) A description of activities planned for the upcoming two quarters.  
    (c) Form.—The information required under subsection (a) may be provided in a written report or a briefing.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that periodic reporting or briefing is a formal consultative process, but the only recipients are the congressional defense committees, which are inside the federal government. The section requires the Navy to give Congress information on physiological episodes in aircraft; it involves no public comment, rulemaking, advisory body with outside members, consultation with non-federal entities, or right to sue. Because every actor is federal, this is not participation.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Navy shall provide to the congressional defense committees information

opus.w: The section only requires the Secretary of the Navy to give recurring briefings or written reports to the congressional defense committees. Both sides of that exchange are inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or granted a right to sue. The formal reporting looks procedural, but it never crosses the federal boundary.
opus.s:
the Secretary of the Navy shall provide to the congressional defense committees information on efforts by the Navy’s Physiological Episode Team to combat the prevalence of 
physiological episodes
opus.b: Someone might read this as participation because the section sets up a recurring, formal flow of information about the Navy's Physiological Episode Team. That reading fails because the only recipients are the congressional defense committees. Congress is inside the federal government, and no state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted before a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of the Navy to provide information to congressional defense committees. Congress is considered inside the federal government, so reporting to it does not constitute participation with outside parties. The subjects of the report (Navy pilots) are federal employees, not outside entities.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the Navy shall provide to the congressional defense committees information on efforts by the Navy’s Physiological Episode Team to combat the prevalence of physiological episodes
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Navy is reporting on efforts to combat physiological episodes, which affects pilots (who are federal employees), there is some form of participation. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are "No" because Congress is inside the federal government. Furthermore, the pilots are federal employees, not outside parties. The section describes a reporting requirement to Congress, not a consultation with outsiders.
